title: 0-shot vs 2-shot: examples teach format — and smuggle bias

events.label: Pose the classification task
events.detail: Classify incoming tickets into refund / billing / inquiry, outputting a single category field.

events.label: The 0-shot call
events.detail: The prompt gives only instructions: "classify the ticket, output JSON {\"category\": string}, values refund/billing/inquiry." No examples at all.

events.label: 0-shot output: format drift
events.detail: {"category": "Refund Request"} — the semantics are right, the literal drifted: capitalized, embellished, neither an agreed enum value.

events.label: 0-shot fails validation
events.detail: Enum match fails: Refund Request ∉ {refund, billing, inquiry}. However clearly the instruction is phrased, format details still rely on the model's guess.

events.label: Inject 2-shot examples
events.detail: Two input → output pairs go into the front of the prompt context: one billing, one inquiry, with outputs written strictly as enum literals like {"category":"billing"}. Placement hardly matters; the paired shape does.

events.label: The 2-shot call
events.detail: Everything else unchanged — the examples are the only new variable.

events.label: Output locks onto the examples
events.detail: {"category":"refund"} — structurally, casing, and enum all match the examples. Examples are output templates: the model imitates their form.

events.label: 2-shot passes validation
events.detail: Enum hit, format locked. From 0-shot to 2-shot, only the examples changed.

events.label: Probe: a trap in the examples
events.detail: Swap in a different example set: both are billing. The refund class is uncovered — watch what happens to generalization.

events.label: Output follows the bias
events.detail: An obvious refund ticket comes back as {"category":"billing"} — all-positive, skewed-class examples lead the model straight into the ditch. Example diversity decides generalization.

events.label: Audit the examples
events.detail: The fix: at least one example per class, cover boundary phrasings, mirror the real distribution. Examples are not casually picked showpieces — they are enforced behavior.

events.label: Conclusion delivered
events.detail: Examples are the most direct behavioral spec — more effective than adjectives, yet they write bias into behavior too. Use few-shot for format-sensitive tasks; skip it for common-sense ones.
